purpose: personal account of how the Kids Horror Stories project grew from a family activity into an automated publishing pipeline

required_facts.fact: The project began when Alexey's son asked for a scary story about a parked car during a walk.
required_facts.evidence: Source lines 20-22: son pointed at a parked car and asked for a horror story; Alexey improvised one.

required_facts.fact: Alexey ran out of ideas after his son began pointing at more objects.
required_facts.evidence: Source line 27: the son pointed at more objects and Alexey eventually ran out of ideas.

required_facts.fact: A photograph of a tree was sent to ChatGPT to generate a story.
required_facts.evidence: Source line 29: Alexey took a photo of the tree and asked ChatGPT for a scary story based on it.

required_facts.fact: The generated tone reminded Alexey of simple urban legends and campfire stories, which children liked.
required_facts.evidence: Source line 29: the tone was simple and sometimes silly, but kids loved it.

required_facts.fact: Alexey and his son spent the rest of that day photographing objects and reading generated stories together.
required_facts.evidence: Source line 31: they took photos of random objects and read the stories together.

required_facts.fact: The first published version was a small Jekyll static site on GitHub Pages.
required_facts.evidence: Source lines 38-40: a static Jekyll project was the fastest option, initially rendering photos and text.

required_facts.fact: The project later automated story, illustration, audio, and podcast generation.
required_facts.evidence: Source line 42: the site evolved into a fully automated pipeline for those outputs.

required_facts.fact: Images can enter through a local folder or an S3 bucket, and GPT-4o generates a story with title and slug.
required_facts.evidence: Source lines 49-54: input image sources and GPT-4o story generation are listed in the architecture.

required_facts.fact: GPT-5 edits Russian grammar and phrasing, while DALL-E 3 creates an illustration from the first one or two paragraphs.
required_facts.evidence: Source lines 52-54: the architecture assigns editing to GPT-5 and illustration generation to DALL-E 3.

required_facts.fact: The site contains more than 1,200 stories, all in Russian.
required_facts.evidence: Source line 8: the site contains 1200+ stories and all stories are in Russian.

author_attribution: Attribute the project and its outcomes to Alexey; preserve the son's role as the source of the initial request and do not invent additional family experiences.
